antiListNotes.fried oils / seed oils: Wallach-direct (Rare Earths, Selenium chapter): 'High intakes of vegetable oils including salad dressing, margarine and cooking oils' drive lipid peroxidation when selenium is low -- 'Age spots / liver spots are indications of a high vegetable oil, low selenium diet', and his Selenium-deficiency table lists 'Alzheimer's Disease -- associated with high vegetable oil consumption' and 'Cancer -- associated with high vegetable oil intake'. (The oft-quoted 'if it has oil in its name don't use it' is a LECTURE line, NOT in the 7 books; 00.A is books-only, so the corpus cites the book verbatim.) High-oleic variants (sunflower/safflower/canola bred for >80% oleic acid) are framework-adjacent -- more oxidation-stable; the engine softens them. Ratified instances (Luneth 2026-08-16): margarine (Wallach-named above); peanut oil + palm oil + palm kernel oil (broad 'vegetable/cooking oil' instances -- Wallach names no positive use; palm is saturated so the omega-6 rationale is weaker, added on the broad stance). EXCLUDED as Wallach-endorsed lipid sources (Rare Earths: 'primary food sources of lipids are butter, flax seed oil, olive oil, animal fat ... olives, avocados, egg yolks'): flax/flaxseed oil, olive oil, fish oil, cod liver oil, avocado oil, butter; coconut oil (Wallach silent, stable saturated). DROPPED on back-check because Wallach speaks POSITIVELY of these -- their oils are NOT flagged: grapeseed (Epigenetics: 'grape-seed extracts have demonstrated protective antioxidant properties'), rice bran (the beriberi 'cure ... essential to health'), and 'shortening' (the Hunza use butter 'as a cooking shortening'). Never blanket-add 'oil'.
antiListNotes.added sugar: Wallach-direct on refined/simple sugar + chromium: 'Dietary sugar loads (colas, apple juice, grape juice, honey, candy, table sugar, fructose, etc.) increase the natural rate of urinary Cr loss by 300% for 12 hours' (Rare Earths; Immortality; Dead Doctors Don't Lie 2011; Epigenetics) -- this verbatim NAMES fructose, so its hard-reject is Wallach-direct. Also 'Simple sugars increase the excretion rate of chromium ... up to 300 percent' (DDDL 2011; Let's Play Doctor 1995). [Back-check 2026-08-16: an earlier edit wrongly dropped the 'Rare Earths / 300% for 12 hours' citation as unverified; it is accurate across 4 books and is restored here.] Two tiers (Luneth-ratified 2026-08-16, 'treat sugar lightly'): HARD-REJECT only the major harmful sources — high fructose corn syrup, corn syrup, fructose ('No fructose', Hell's Kitchen p.258 sugar-elimination list). Every other added sugar is a MINOR (mild) flag, never a reject — this category is deliberately NOT in seriousAnti, so cane sugar / evaporated cane juice / cane juice / dextrose / maltodextrin / sucrose (= table sugar) / molasses / brown sugar / turbinado read as worth-knowing flags whose severity scales with exposure, not 'avoid'. Mild-tier terms trace to Wallach's Hell's Kitchen p.258 'No ___' list ('No table sugar', 'No molasses (cane juice, turbanado sugar, brown sugar, etc.)'). Label terms use correct real-world spellings (turbinado, not Wallach's OCR 'turbanado'). HELD for Luneth's call, not added: honey (direct 'No honey' but Wallach bakes with it), maple syrup + agave (no Wallach verbatim), apple/grape juice (broad).
antiListNotes.artificial sweeteners: Wallach accepts sucralose (Hell's Kitchen: 'Splenda (also known as Sucralose)... used in moderation ... considered safe' — and it sweetens dozens of his own recipes), so sucralose is deliberately NOT flagged — removed from the anti-list (Luneth 2026-08-16). Aspartame and acesulfame are mainstream-controversial — framework-adjacent, kept as hard-rejects. Stevia is Wallach-friendly.
antiListNotes.caffeine: Wallach-direct: caffeine raises urinary Cr loss for ~12 hrs per dose. Not anti-coffee absolute, but flag for Cr cofactor balance.
antiListNotes.gluten sources: Wallach-direct on actual gluten proteins: wheat / barley / rye / malt / spelt — these are an unconditional hard reject regardless of marketing (a gluten source is never a 'save'). Oats flag by default (commercial supply chains carry cross-contamination risk). Operational rule: if ANY oat ingredient in the label is declared 'gluten-free' — in either word order ('gluten free oats' or 'oats (gluten free)') — ALL oat-derivatives in that product are presumed GF, because a brand certifying one oat ingredient operates in a GF-aware supply chain across the rest. A 'gluten-free' claim attached to a NON-oat ingredient (e.g., 'gluten-free pasta') does NOT certify oats. Hard gluten proteins appearing elsewhere still flag independently — no shutoff trick. Buckwheat is a pseudocereal, gluten-free despite the name. Ratified instances (Luneth 2026-08-16): triticale/semolina/durum/farina/graham/seitan/einkorn/kamut/bulgur/couscous/farro are all wheat- or gluten-protein grains -- same unconditional hard reject (wheat germ/bran/starch/flour and malt-* are already caught by the 'wheat'/'malt' word-match, so not duplicated). Second ratified batch (Luneth 2026-08-16): emmer (Wallach's own 'emmer wheat') / freekeh / panko / orzo / matzo / maida / atta -- wheat grains + wheat products, same unconditional hard reject; none was caught by the existing 'wheat' word-match. Skipped: udon (Wallach uses buckwheat udon in a recipe -- a nuance, not blanket gluten). panko/orzo have rare gluten-free reformulations that still hard-reject, consistent with 'a gluten source is never a save'.
antiListNotes.msg / glutamate: Wallach: free glutamate is a neurotoxin concern. Common hidden sources: yeast extract, hydrolyzed protein. Ratified instances (Luneth 2026-08-16): autolyzed yeast (= yeast extract), hydrolyzed vegetable/soy protein (specifiers of 'hydrolyzed protein'), and glutamic acid + monopotassium glutamate (direct free glutamate like MSG). Reviewed against all 7 books and DROPPED (Luneth 2026-08-16): textured vegetable protein / caseinate / torula yeast — Wallach names none (torula: 0 book hits; caseinate: 0 hits, only bare 'casein' cited neutrally as a protein/amino-acid source; 'textured vegetable protein': 0 hits, and Wallach speaks POSITIVELY of vegetable protein). The genuinely glutamate-bearing hydrolyzed forms are already covered by hydrolyzed vegetable/soy protein, so these three would be counter-Wallach outside-knowledge entries.
antiListNotes.modified / processed: Wallach is broadly anti-processed/refined food: 'no processed or white flours', 'processed white flour and sugar' (empty-calorie diets), and 'processed salt confuses the body' (Dead Doctors Don't Lie, 2011); 'genetically modified' is his 'Frankenstein Food' (DDDL). Modified starches (modified food / corn / tapioca starch) are refined/processed derivatives, so this maps Wallach's anti-processed stance onto 'modified' ingredients. NOTE: no Wallach verbatim uses the word 'modified' for an ingredient — this is an inference awaiting Luneth's severity ratification (serious flag vs unconditional hard reject). Ratified instances (Luneth 2026-08-16): enriched flour, bleached flour, white flour ('no processed or white flours'), and refined -- refined/processed flour derivatives (modified-* starches are already caught by the 'modified' word-match).
